title: Signature Database Ablation Study
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Ablation and Feature Contribution Experiments Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. The Signature edition does not copy any public product: it restates the subject in Manon's own Signature framing, as a design that lives inside the Signature ecosystem. Database Ablation Study covers the following in Signature terms: measures the score change when one database is removed from the retrieval set. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Benchmark honesty: this database defines part of the fixed test suite for the R32 capability collection. Its target is 99% measured reliability on defined tasks (TARGET, not measured result). The comparative measurement run comes after building and is not claimed anywhere in this round.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: an ablation run holds the task list and every other feature fixed, removes exactly one feature, and records the resulting score beside the full-configuration score, so the difference in score points is attributable to that one feature alone. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: measures the score change when one database is removed from the retrieval set. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo compares a full configuration score with an ablated configuration score and prints the difference in score points. The demo program prints:

Full configuration score: 80 points
Ablated configuration score: 78 points
Feature contribution: 2 score points

Use and limits

Ablation scores describe the tested configuration only. Removing two features at once can behave differently from removing either alone, and interaction effects need their own dedicated studies. In Signature practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check inside the Signature ecosystem: follow the design, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this Signature database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here.

Record details

Record fields: feature_removed: verification step; configuration: ablated configuration; metric: cost per task; task_class: retrieval of existing records.

It restates only the generic method of this subject in Signature terms, so that Signature users share one clear starting point.

print('Feature contribution: ' + str(contribution) + ' score points')
